entities.summary:
Alban of Mainz was a Catholic priest, missionary, and martyr in the Late Roman Empire. He was born into a Christian family in Rome, Italy, around 350-360 CE and was raised in the Christian faith. Alban's family was of noble origin, and he was educated in theology and philosophy.

In 378 CE, Alban, then a deacon, was ordained as a priest by Bishop Ambrosius of Trier. He was known for his piety, charity, and kindness, earning him the respect and admiration of his community. Alban was also a skilled healer and was often called upon to minister to the sick and the poor.

When the Roman Emperor Valens was defeated by the Goths in 378 CE, Alban was martyred for his Christian faith. According to legend, Alban was beheaded by the Roman soldiers in the city of Mainz, Germany, and was buried in a secret location. His remains were later discovered and reburied in the Mainz Cathedral, where he was canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church.

Alban of Mainz's legacy extends beyond his own time and place. He is venerated as a saint and a martyr in the Catholic Church, and his feast day is celebrated on June 22. His story has inspired countless works of art, literature, and music, and he remains a beloved figure in Christian tradition. Alban's commitment to his faith and his selfless service to others serve as a powerful reminder of the importance of compassion, kindness, and devotion.
